PullRequest.Title: Present Copilot Fusion when CAPI returns unavailable Fusion tiers
PullRequest.Body:
<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:
  https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.

On accounts whose plan can't run Fusion, such as Copilot Free, the Agent Host model picker showed plain **Auto** instead of **Copilot Fusion**. This PR makes it show Copilot Fusion, with the Fusion tiers marked unavailable.

CAPI returns the Fusion tiers to these accounts as disabled. Agent Host logs from a Free account show:

```
Provider Auto tiers: default 'balance'; balance (auto), hydrafusion (fusion, disabled), hydrafusion-max (fusion, disabled), fast (auto)
Auto presentation: Auto with CAPI's tiers, no Fusion: ... [hydrafusion=disabled (This tier is not available for the user's Copilot plan.), ...]
```

The Fusion presentation was gated on a Fusion tier the account could run, so these accounts fell back to plain Auto.

## Change

`offersFusionAutoTier` now checks whether CAPI returned any Fusion tier that's visible in the picker, not whether the tier is enabled. This changes:
- Auto is presented as **Copilot Fusion** whenever CAPI returns a Fusion tier.
- Tiers the account can't run appear in the Effort Level picker as unavailable, through the existing auto-tier `_meta`.

These stay the same:
- When CAPI returns no Fusion tier, the picker still shows Auto with "Optimize for".
- HydraFusion is still added as a separate model only for tiers the account can run.
- Only enabled tiers can be selected.

The `Auto presentation` log messages are updated to match.

## Testing

The test that asserted plain Auto when Fusion tiers came back disabled now covers three cases:
- Fusion tiers unavailable: Copilot Fusion with High and Max unavailable, and no HydraFusion models.
- Account that lists no models (Free): the host's own Auto entry is presented as Copilot Fusion.
- No Fusion tier from CAPI: still Auto.

Run on this branch with Node 24.22.1:
- `npm run test-node -- --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotAgent.test.ts --run src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotSessionLauncher.test.ts`: passed (1135 passing, 0 failing)
- `npm run eslint -- src/vs/platform/agentHost/node/copilot/copilotAgent.ts src/vs/platform/agentHost/test/node/copilotAgent.test.ts`: passed

Not run: manual UI check with a signed-in Free account.

Fixes #344788

Scenarios.Scenario: Authenticated startup or scheduled Copilot model-catalog refresh, followed by model-picker publication
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The refresh waits for the Copilot client, models.list, managed-settings resolution, synchronous projection of M models and T Auto tiers, and publication. The changed offersFusionAutoTier predicate executes only after the remote catalog is available; for unavailable Fusion it changes the single Auto row's name/schema/meta decoration but adds no wait or boundary. Publication then schedules the same existing model-configuration refresh for each live chat session.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Ensure/start the Copilot SDK client used for model discovery
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one client start when the shared client is absent; subsequent warm refreshes reuse it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same client startup/reuse path ran before the predicate change.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required before the model catalog can be listed on a cold client.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: List Copilot models and Auto-tier metadata via client.rpc.models.list
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One call per refresh attempt; failure retries are sequential and bounded by the existing retry policy.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Exactly one models.list call per attempt before the diff as well.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The catalog cannot be published until this call completes.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve managed model settings after a successful model listing
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One resolution per successful refresh attempt.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same policy resolution was already on the refresh critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Refresh each live session's model configuration with session.model.list and session.model.getCurrent
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two control-plane RPCs per live session after each existing catalog publication; each session sequences its own refreshes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: _publishModels already iterated every live session and queued the same refresh regardless of whether unavailable Fusion tiers presented Auto as Fusion.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the catalog publication's synchronous critical path because refreshModelConfiguration queues asynchronous work, though it consumes IPC proportional to live sessions.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: M returned models, T provider Auto tiers, and S live chat sessions. The changed predicate remains O(T), and the new presentation allocation is bounded to the single Auto model; existing publication work remains O(M + T + S).
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Public refreshModels calls coalesce onto one in-flight refresh, invalidating lifecycle triggers coalesce onto one next-task refresh, and failures retry sequentially with backoff. Per-session configuration refreshes are queued by each session; aggregate concurrency can scale with S, but the diff does not add publications or session refreshes.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The last-known catalog is retained on refresh failure, model refreshes are coalesced, and the same provider metadata is reused during publication. The diff changes neither cache keys nor cold/warm refresh behavior and adds no positive or negative cache state.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: both offersFusionAutoTier call sites and the full publication/session-refresh path were traced; the before/after difference is only predicate eligibility and resulting in-memory presentation metadata.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Actual catalog sizes and live-session counts vary, but the changed work is a tiny bounded transformation of one Auto row and does not change the dominant remote or per-session operation counts.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The PR does not add or fan out any expensive boundary and does not increase refresh frequency; it only chooses the existing Fusion presentation branch for metadata that was already fetched and published.

Scenarios.Scenario: Model discovery for an alternate scoped credential source
Scenarios.CriticalPath: On a cold scoped-catalog entry, the host starts a temporary scoped Copilot runtime, lists models, resolves managed settings, projects the model list (including the changed Fusion predicate), and then stops the runtime. The caller waits for this entire sequence.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Start and stop a temporary ScopedCopilotClient runtime
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One start and one stop per cold scoped-catalog creation; shared calls for the same source use one promise.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The temporary runtime lifecycle was identical before the presentation predicate changed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Both startup and shutdown are awaited by scoped discovery.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: List models through the scoped runtime
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One models.list call per cold scoped-catalog creation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same single catalog request occurred before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required before scoped models can be returned.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve managed settings for the scoped credential
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One resolution per cold scoped-catalog creation.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same resolution was already awaited.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Returned models wait for policy resolution.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: M models and T Auto tiers for one credential source. The presentation check remains O(T) and decorates at most the one Auto model; no extra remote request is caused.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Calls for the same source/current credential/startup configuration share the cached promise. Different credential sources may discover in parallel as before; the diff adds no concurrency or limiter bypass.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The scoped catalog/promise is cached by source and reused while credentials and startup configuration remain current. Cancellation without a completed catalog can recreate it. The changed predicate neither changes the cache key nor invalidates the entry.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the scoped cache ownership, temporary runtime lifecycle, and _presentModels call were directly inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of simultaneous credential sources is product-dependent, but same-source coalescing and all expensive operation counts are unchanged.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The diff changes only how already-returned metadata labels the Auto row and does not alter scoped runtime, request, cache, or concurrency behavior.

Scenarios.Scenario: In-memory model republishing after BYOK registry changes or local-model row changes
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The trigger reads cached/local model rows, rebuilds and publishes the merged model array, then queues existing per-session model-configuration refreshes. BYOK publication may separately synchronize BYOK registrations to active sessions. The changed predicate can choose Fusion decoration during the synchronous rebuild but introduces no new trigger or publication.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Per-session model.list and model.getCurrent during queued model-configuration refresh
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Two RPCs per active session for each publication, sequenced within each session.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Every _publishModels call already queued these same per-session refreshes; the predicate result does not control that loop.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Queued after synchronous publication and therefore off the immediate picker-update path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Synchronize BYOK model registrations to active sessions when BYOK rows are present
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One sync attempt per active session on qualifying BYOK refreshes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The BYOK session-sync loop and its cardinality are unchanged.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: M catalog/BYOK/local rows and S active sessions. Existing work scales O(M + S); the changed branch adds a constant-size copy for the single Auto row and no additional S-scaled operation.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each trigger calls _publishModels synchronously. Session model-configuration work is queued per session, while BYOK registration may run across active sessions; these scheduling rules and trigger counts are unchanged by the diff.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: BYOK models come from the bridge registry's cached serving window, and unchanged root config values suppress redundant BYOK refreshes. Local rows are read from the current provider. Fusion eligibility uses already-held Auto-tier metadata; no new cache miss or external fetch occurs.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: all _publishModels calls touched by local/BYOK changes and the transitive session refresh implementation were traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Large active-session counts make the pre-existing publication fan-out more expensive, but this PR neither increases publication frequency nor adds a session-level call.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The only new cost on this path is bounded object spreading/localization for one Auto presentation; all session-scaled IPC is pre-existing and occurs at the same frequency.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over both changed files and all diff pages. Traced both Fusion-predicate call sites, downstream workbench metadata consumption, normal and scoped model discovery, publication, and per-session refresh fan-out. No high-confidence performance regression or qualifying regression fix was found.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
